clue.text: Part of the EU said to be after joint effort

indicators.note: to be after places the sound-alike piece behind the joint in the answer

parts.note: the elbow is the joint in the middle of the arm

indicators.note: said tells us to take how the country's name sounds when spoken

parts.note: Greece is a member state of the European Union

explanation.surface: A jumbled remark about a member of the EU joining in on a shared European project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint effort' reads as one phrase meaning teamwork, but 'joint' is the wordplay and 'effort' alone is the definition. 'said' gives GREASE from Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: Elbow grease is the idiom for hard physical labour, such as vigorous scrubbing or polishing.

clue.text: Involve team regularly with grill in America

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the word team

parts.note: broil is the American word for grilling food under direct heat

explanation.surface: A request to bring a sports squad along to an American barbecue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' picks the 2nd and 4th letters of 'team', E and M.
explanation.definitionFit: To embroil someone is to drag them into a conflict or difficult situation, a stronger synonym of involve.

clue.text: Disappointments resulting in fisticuffs?

definitions.meaning: setbacks or shocks, as in 'a bitter blow'
a fight with fists, a series of punches

explanation.surface: Letdowns that end in a brawl.
explanation.definitionFit: A setback is called a blow, and the punches thrown in a fistfight are likewise blows.

clue.text: Wretched internet with nothing in, for example on energy

indicators.note: in means the nothing letter goes inside the internet word

parts.note: the web is a common name for the internet
O is the digit zero, nothing
eg is the abbreviation of exempli gratia, for example
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A miserable person complaining about the internet and its energy use.
explanation.definitionFit: Woebegone describes someone looking sorrowful and miserable, a near-synonym of wretched.

clue.text: Ring around which sheep wander

indicators.note: around means the sheep word sits on either side of the ring letter

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep
O is shaped like a ring

explanation.surface: A circular pen around which the flock roams freely.
explanation.definitionFit: To roam is to travel aimlessly over a wide area, a synonym of wander.

clue.text: High German, but without British rationale

indicators.note: high in the sense of drunk or intoxicated, so the letters stagger into a new order
without means the British letter is taken away from the fodder before rearranging

explanation.surface: A puzzling remark about the High German language with the British left out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High German' looks like the language, but 'High' is the anagram signal; GERMANBUT less B gives GERMANUT, which rearranges into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An argument is a reasoned case set out to justify something, which is what a rationale provides.

clue.text: Applaud as former sale item turned up

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue means the sale item word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a lot is an item offered at auction

explanation.surface: Clapping when a previously sold item resurfaces at auction.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to praise highly, a figurative way of applauding someone.

clue.text: One of the Krays perhaps fixed something to wear

parts.note: Ronnie and Reggie Kray were identical twin gangsters in 1960s London; perhaps marks them as an example
set means fixed, as in a set price

explanation.surface: A notorious East End gangster rigging something in his wardrobe.
explanation.walkthrough: The Krays were twin brothers who ran organised crime in London's East End. A twinset is a matching jumper and cardigan, a classic British outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: A twinset is a matching knitted jumper and cardigan worn together, clearly an item of clothing.

clue.text: Rest may be about to interrupt swimmer

indicators.note: to interrupt means the about word breaks into the middle of the swimmer word

parts.note: a bather is someone swimming in the sea or a pool
re means about or concerning, as in business letters

explanation.surface: A swimmer is about to be interrupted, perhaps to take a pause.
explanation.definitionFit: A breather is a short pause for rest, time to catch one's breath.

clue.text: Recoil as room began spinning

indicators.note: spinning means the letters of room began whirl round into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone staggers back as the room starts to spin.
explanation.definitionFit: To boomerang is to come back on the one who started it, rebounding just as a recoil does.

clue.text: Sailors must have source of iodine for these bones

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor

indicators.note: source of means taking the opening letter of iodine

explanation.surface: Seamen need iodine supplements to keep their bones healthy.
explanation.definitionFit: The tarsi are the small bones of the ankle and upper foot; the plural matches 'these bones'.

clue.text: School inspectors needing university for female getting expelled

indicators.note: for means the university letter replaces the female letter

parts.note: Ofsted is the body that inspects schools in England

explanation.surface: Inspectors call in a university to deal with a woman who is being thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: OFSTED, the Office for Standards in Education, inspects English schools.
explanation.definitionFit: Ousted means forced out of a position, a close synonym of expelled.

clue.text: Announcements from shopping centre taken in by unhappy son

indicators.note: taken in by means the shopping centre word goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: sad means unhappy
a mall is a shopping centre

explanation.surface: Adverts from the shopping centre lapped up by a gloomy young man.
explanation.walkthrough: MALL goes after the first S of SADS.
explanation.definitionFit: Small ads are the short classified notices in a newspaper, announcing items for sale or wanted.

clue.text: Not having so much to do may be an example

parts.note: less means a smaller amount
on means happening, as in 'what's on' or something to do

explanation.surface: Having less to do might serve as a model for others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to do' gives ON in the sense of an event taking place.
explanation.definitionFit: A lesson can be a salutary warning, as in 'let that be a lesson to you', meaning an example to learn from.

clue.text: Plan new target in case of supply

indicators.note: in means the rearranged letters go inside the outer letters
case of means the outside letters of supply, like a container holding something
new means the letters of target are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A business plan to hit a new target for supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case of' means only the outside letters of 'supply' are used, here acting as a container.
explanation.definitionFit: A strategy is a long-term plan of action designed to achieve a goal.

clue.text: Picture crack and go

parts.note: snap means crack, the sharp sound of something breaking
shot means a go or try, as in 'have a shot'

explanation.surface: Someone pictures breaking something and leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: A snapshot is an informal photograph taken quickly, a kind of picture.

clue.text: Paired off, sacking one politician getting greedy

indicators.note: off in the sense of gone bad, so the letters are spoiled into a new order
sacking means the letter for one is dismissed from the fodder

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A paired-up politician is fired and turns out to be grasping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sacking one' drops I from PAIRED, leaving PARED, and 'off' turns it into PREDA. A Tory is a British Conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: Predatory describes preying on others for gain, and figuratively means rapacious and greedy.

clue.text: Learned people could be a bit politer at introductions

indicators.note: a bit means the answer is a small piece taken from inside the words politer at introductions

explanation.surface: Intellectuals might be a little more courteous when introducing people.
explanation.definitionFit: The literati are educated people interested in literature, the well-read intelligentsia.

clue.text: Bush may see refusal mostly after backing newspaper

indicators.note: after means the refusal piece follows the newspaper piece
backing means the newspaper word is turned round from back to front

parts.note: rag is a slang term for a poor-quality newspaper

indicators.note: mostly means the refusal word loses its final letter

parts.note: a denial is a refusal

explanation.surface: A politician named Bush meets a mostly negative response from a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bush' wants to be the US president; it is a shrub. 'backing' turns RAG to GAR; 'mostly' cuts DENIAL to DENIA.
explanation.definitionFit: The gardenia is an evergreen shrub with fragrant white flowers, so it is a kind of bush.

clue.text: His finish is a stroke of luck

parts.note: with a capital H, His refers to God, so His means God's
end means finish

explanation.surface: A man's ending turns out to be fortunate.
explanation.walkthrough: A capitalised 'His' or 'He' conventionally refers to God; the apostrophe of GOD'S is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: A godsend is an unexpected piece of good fortune, something that arrives just when needed.

clue.text: Angrily condemn the Tour de France?

definitions.meaning: to speak out furiously against something, to rant
read in French, the definite article le plus a word for tour gives '...', a playful French rendering of the tour

explanation.surface: Fury aimed at the famous cycle race.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is cryptic: LE is French for 'the' and TRIP means tour, so 'le trip' is 'the tour' in mock French.
explanation.definitionFit: To let rip means to speak or act without restraint, especially in a burst of anger at someone.

clue.text: Inventor needing individual in support

indicators.note: in means the individual word sits inside the support word

parts.note: a pier is a pillar supporting a bridge or arch
one means a single individual

explanation.surface: An inventor needs a single person to back him up.
explanation.definitionFit: A pioneer is the first to develop a new method or field, which is what an inventor does.

clue.text: Hated action taken about evaluation

indicators.note: taken about means the action word is put around the evaluation word

parts.note: a deed is an action
a test is an evaluation

explanation.surface: A disliked course of action follows an assessment.
explanation.definitionFit: Detested means loathed intensely, a strong synonym of hated.

clue.text: Head of this involved in leak that's expensive

indicators.note: involved in means the head letter is placed inside the leak word

parts.note: to seep is to leak slowly

indicators.note: Head of means the first letter of the word this

explanation.surface: A boss caught up in a costly leak.
explanation.definitionFit: Steep is the informal word for prices that are unreasonably high, meaning costly.

clue.text: Bob, say, making hospital radio broadcast

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

indicators.note: broadcast in the sense of scattered, so the letters of radio are strewn into a new order

explanation.surface: A man called Bob is putting on a hospital radio programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' looks like a presenter's name; it is a haircut, with 'say' marking it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A bob is a short haircut, one example of a styled arrangement of the hair.

clue.text: Rear level for the audience

indicators.note: for the audience means we take how the level word sounds to listeners

parts.note: to raze a building is to level it to the ground

explanation.surface: Instructions about a stage: lift the rear, level for the spectators.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rear' looks like a noun meaning the back; it is the verb, to bring up.
explanation.definitionFit: To rear children or animals is to bring them up, and raise is the common synonym.

clue.text: Book token

definitions.meaning: the Gospel of St ... is a book of the New Testament

explanation.definitionFit: Mark is a New Testament gospel, and a mark is also a sign or token of something.

clue.text: Flyer, keen to finish early holds line

indicators.note: holds means the shortened word contains the line letter
to finish early means the keen word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: eager means keen

explanation.surface: An eager pilot wanting to land early stays in the queue.
explanation.walkthrough: EAGER loses its R, then L goes in before the final E.
explanation.definitionFit: An eagle is a large bird of prey, and in crosswords a flyer is anything that flies.

clue.text: Working with Italian in a fury to get this mineral

indicators.note: in means the two pieces go inside the fury pieces

parts.note: rage means fury
on means working or operating, as in a machine being on
It is an abbreviation for Italian, as in It vermouth

explanation.surface: Someone working with an Italian flies into a rage to obtain a rock sample.
explanation.definitionFit: Aragonite is a crystalline form of calcium carbonate, a naturally occurring mineral named after Aragon in Spain.

clue.text: Fruit offered by waspish couple on the radio

parts.note: waspish and prickly both mean irritable and quick to take offence

indicators.note: on the radio means we take how the couple word sounds when broadcast

parts.note: a pair is a couple

explanation.surface: A tetchy married pair offer some fruit during a radio show.
explanation.definitionFit: The prickly pear is the edible fruit of the opuntia cactus.
